transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, they said I had to come in after the fair. I was supposed to be giving a talk, you know, about the equipment and patterns in the field—people don’t always understand how the rows line up, there’s a way to see it if you’ve worked land long enough.

Anyway, I got up on the tractor during it and started moving the controls, jerking them back and forth to show everybody the new pattern. Folks were yelling at me to stop, and I heard them, I did, but I just… couldn’t make myself stop right then. So that’s why they brought me here, I guess.

Can you tell me more about what was going through your mind while you were moving the tractor controls back and forth? Did you feel like something was controlling you or that you had to do it for a specific reason?

I don’t know if I’d say something was controlling me. It was more like… I had to show them the pattern, the way the tractor was supposed to move. Folks don’t understand unless they see it, and I was trying to make it clear.

I got up there during the talk and started moving the controls back and forth, and then people were hollering for me to stop. I heard them, but my hands just kept going. It’s like when you’re fixing a fence and you know one post is off—you can’t leave it be till it lines up right. I couldn’t make myself stop right then, even though everybody was yelling.
While you were moving the tractor controls, did you feel like something outside of yourself—like a voice or a force—was making you do it, or did it feel like it was completely your own idea?

It felt like my idea, I guess… not like a voice telling me. I just knew they needed to see that new pattern, how the tractor was supposed to move.

I got up there during my talk at the fair and started jerking the controls back and forth, and once I started, I couldn’t seem to stop—even with everybody yelling. It was like I was trying to make the rows line up in my head, you know, like when the irrigation runs crooked and then you start thinking about the old south field and how my dad used to say you can’t teach people by just pointing at dirt… but no, it wasn’t some outside force. It was me trying to show them.
While you were moving the tractor controls back and forth, were you fully aware of what you were doing, or did things feel foggy or unreal to you at all?

I was aware, mostly. I knew I was up on that tractor and I knew my hands were on the controls, jerking them back and forth. It wasn’t like I was asleep or gone somewhere.

It’s just… once I got started showing them that new pattern, I couldn’t make myself stop, even with folks yelling. The fair had all that noise, and people crowding around, and I kept thinking if they’d just watch the movement they’d understand. Kind of like when you’re trying to explain a fence line to someone who’s never walked it—well, anyway, I knew what I was doing, but I wasn’t stopping like I should’ve.
While you were moving the tractor controls, did it feel like you were on autopilot or that you were watching yourself do it, like it wasn’t quite you doing it?

Not like watching myself from across the room, no. I knew it was me up there. But it did sort of feel like once I got going, my hands just kept at it, back and forth on those controls, like I had to finish showing the crowd that new pattern.

That’s why they brought me in, I guess. I climbed onto that tractor during my talk at the fair, and people were yelling, but I couldn’t make myself stop right then. I kept thinking, if they’d just see the movement, they’d understand. It’s like trying to show somebody how a gate swings wrong—well, my uncle had one that never latched right—but anyway, it was me doing it. I just couldn’t quit when I should’ve.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts were being put into your mind by someone else, taken out of your mind, or broadcast out loud for others to hear?

I don’t know about thoughts being put in or taken out exactly… not like that. But I do feel like certain things are meant for me to catch, and other people don’t see it.

Like my wife will put the lender’s paperwork in front of me and say, “See, it’s plain numbers, it’s just the loan papers,” but the odd numbers in the yield maps, and those drone reports—those aren’t just numbers. They’re coded warnings. Folks are trying to take the farm out from under me.

And I’ve tried explaining that, but then we get off into whether the north pasture ever produced right after the hail year, and nobody wants to talk about that either. But no, I can see the warnings in there. That part I’m sure of.
Do you believe that the coded warnings you see in the paperwork and drone reports are specifically meant for you and that others are actively trying to deceive or harm you through them?

Yes. I mean, I know how it sounds when you say it back like that, but yes, those warnings are meant for me. My wife keeps pointing at the lender papers like they’re just regular figures, just interest and payments and all that, but that’s not where it is.

It’s the odd numbers in the yield maps, and the drone reports too. Those don’t line up by accident. They’re telling me folks are moving on the farm, trying to take it out from under me. And people act like I’m making too much of it, but I’ve worked that land long enough to know when something’s off. Like when a field looks fine from the road but you walk it and see the low spots—anyway, yes, I believe it’s aimed at me.
Have you ever believed something was happening or being done to you that others would say is not possible or does not make sense, even if you were sure it was real at the time?

Yes… I mean, others say it doesn’t make sense. My wife especially, she’ll lay those lender papers out in front of me and say, “Look, it’s just plain numbers.” But I know what I’m seeing.

It’s not the regular paperwork so much. It’s the odd numbers in the yield maps, and those drone reports—those are coded warnings. They’re meant to tell me people are trying to take the farm out from under me. And I know folks say, “That’s not possible,” but after you’ve worked land long enough, you notice patterns other people miss. Like weather coming in before the radio says it—anyway, yes, I was sure it was real.
Have you ever believed something was happening to you that you know might sound impossible or hard to believe, like something completely outside the normal rules of how things work?

Yeah… I know it sounds hard to believe when I say it out loud. But I’ve told you, even when my wife puts the lender’s papers right in front of me and says it’s all plain numbers, I can’t just ignore what I’m seeing.

It’s the odd numbers in the yield maps, and the drone reports too. Those aren’t just random. They’re coded warnings. Like when you’re checking a fence line and something’s just… off, even if nobody else sees it from the truck. I know folks are trying to take the farm out from under me. Others may say that’s not how things work, but to me it’s clear.
Have you ever believed something was happening to you that you know might sound completely impossible or illogical, even to the point where you yourself questioned whether it made sense at all?

Yeah… yes, I have. I mean, there are moments where I’ll look at it and think, “Now, why would somebody put a warning in a yield map?” That sounds… I know how it sounds. My wife will put the lender’s paperwork right there on the kitchen table and say it’s plain as day, just ordinary numbers and terms.

But then I see the odd numbers in the yield maps, and the drone reports have the same kind of thing, and I can’t shake it. It feels like they’re coded warnings, like folks are trying to take the farm out from under me. I’ll question it for a second, sure, but then it lines up in my head again. Kind of like when a calf acts wrong before you can see what’s wrong with it—anyway, yes, even when part of me knows it may not make sense, I still believe it.
Have you ever believed something was happening to you that you yourself recognized as completely implausible or impossible, even while you were experiencing it?

Yeah… I recognized it sounded impossible, sure. I’d sit there with my wife at the table, and she’d have the lender papers spread out, pointing at the numbers like, “See, it’s just normal paperwork.” And part of me would think, well… maybe that’s what it looks like.

But then I’d go back to the yield maps, or those drone reports, and the odd numbers weren’t just odd to me. They felt like coded warnings. Like somebody was telling me, in a roundabout way, that folks were trying to take the farm out from under me.

And I know that sounds… not how things work. But farming’s full of things folks miss if they don’t know what they’re looking at. You see a patch in a field, or the way cattle bunch up before a storm, and city people say you’re imagining it—anyway. Yes. Even when I could tell it sounded completely implausible, I still felt sure about it.
